name: What is the cheapest way to add space to a house?

mainEntity.name: What is the cheapest way to add usable space to a house in Los Angeles without a full addition?
mainEntity.text: What is the cheapest way to add usable space to a house in Los Angeles without a full addition?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the goal is to add functional space at the lowest cost, the best option is often to use existing square footage more efficiently or build a small, simple expansion. A bump-out may cost less than a full room addition because it adds only a limited area and usually avoids major layout changes. Converting a garage, attic, or underused interior space can sometimes be even more economical if zoning and code requirements allow it. Costs rise quickly when plumbing, HVAC, foundation work, or roof modifications are involved. Homeowners should compare the cost per usable function, not just cost per square foot. A smaller project that adds a bedroom or office with minimal structural work may produce better value than a larger custom addition. The cheapest option is not always the best resale choice, so the layout, permits, and intended use should guide the decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: The cheapest way to add space is usually a small bump-out, conversion of existing space, or a compact ground-level addition with minimal plumbing and structural changes. Projects become much cheaper when they avoid moving major systems, expanding foundations, or changing the roofline.
